title: Artifactory. Sensing and photonic engineering.
description: Meet the company-level focus connecting ArtiSense sensing research and AIFIELD design tools, with clear evidence and collaboration paths.
lead: Explore the work through the questions it addresses: how to sense with light, and how to design the systems that make that possible.

sections.title: A company presented through its work.
paragraphs: Artifactory is the company behind the two projects presented here. The proposed positioning connects sensing technology with tools for designing photonic systems. It gives investors and potential collaborators a way to assess the work at a company level.
The site concentrates on ArtiSense and AIFIELD. Their pages describe different purposes, stages and evidence boundaries rather than a single combined product.

sections.title: Related work, distinct responsibilities.
paragraphs: ArtiSense pursues a miniaturized chemical-sensing concept using photonics and signal interpretation. AIFIELD addresses photonic design and simulation, alongside a separate neural field research direction.

The internal glucose-related design example links an intended sensing objective to an engineering workflow. That connection does not make a simulated design a validated sensor, and the two projects’ neural subjects are not the same technology.

sections.title: Read the date with the claim.
paragraphs: The supplied context describes optical feasibility and chip-design work for ArtiSense. AIFIELD capability descriptions refer to a September 2026 snapshot. These provide a basis for a technical conversation while leaving current availability and further validation to be confirmed.
The approach page explains how concept, simulation and physical evidence should be distinguished. Project evidence pages keep the limits attached to the work they describe.

sections.title: Choose the conversation that fits.
paragraphs: Investors can begin with the company proposition and its unresolved development questions. Potential collaborators can start from a measurement, design or evaluation topic. A non-confidential introduction is enough for the first enquiry.
Use the contact page to describe your interest and preferred context. It provides an editable enquiry form and a public email route.
